Vide this judgment/award, this Tribunal shall decide petition/application/DAR filed for compensation on account of the injuries sustained by injured Ajay Pal Singh in a road vehicular accident which took place on 4/5.08.2017 at about 00:15AM at Yamuna Expressway, KM48-500 RHS from Agra to Ajay Pal Singh vs Ram Chandra & ors. MACT No.381/2018 Page no.3 of 25 HARVINDER by HARVINDER SINGH SINGH Date: 2024.03.11 17:04:15 +0530
texts.facts: CASE OF THE PETITIONER SIDE 2. Succinctly, the case put forth vide petition/application/DAR is that in the midnight of 04/05.08.2017, Ajay Pal Singh was on patrolling duty with other people of his team on Yamuna Expressway in vehicle PRV5 Mahindra Pickup. They were all posted at Yamuna Expressway, Jever Toll Plaza, Uttar Pradesh. They reached at KM48 500 RHS of Yamuna Expressway as they had information about one punctured Truck bearing registration no. RJ11GA4230 standing still at the spot. Petitioner and other members of team were putting safety cones & barricades on the road. In the meantime, Canter bearing registration no. DL1M7272 came from Agra side and hit the said stagnant Truck. Information was given to Jever Toll Plaza. Some more barricades, an ambulance, a pickup Van and a fire tender were called at the spot for safety measures. Safety measures were taken. Ajay Pal and some other persons were in process of pulling the Canter to one side vide Crane. At about 00:15 hours, one another Canter bearing registration No. DL1LS4071 came at a very high speed, in rash manner, in negligent manner and hit the safety instruments and barricades. In said incident, Mahindra pickup, one fire tender, Canter No. DL1M7272 and ambulance were damaged. Petitioner also sustained injuries in said incident. Injured along with other victims of the incident were shifted to J. P. Hospital, Uttar Pradesh. The incident took place due to rash and negligent driving of driver of the offending vehicle bearing registration No. DL1LS4071. He was working as Driver and was earning Ajay Pal Singh vs Ram Chandra & ors. MACT No.381/2018 Page no.4 of 25 HARVINDER by HARVINDER SINGH SINGH Date: 2024.03.11 17:04:19 +0530 Ajay Pal Singh -/- vs Ram Chandra on 7 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124711287/ 3 Rs.16,500/- per month at the time of incident. The respondent no.01 being LR of driver, respondent no.02 being owner and respondent no.03 being insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to petitioner. The injured/petitioner/claimant has sought compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- (Rupees Fifty Lakhs Only) from the respondents. MISCELLANEOUS PROCEEDINGS 3. Notice of the application/DAR was issued to the respondents, they appeared and filed their written statement(s)/reply(ies) to the present application/petition/DAR. 4.1 In gist, the response of the respondents no.01 & 02 as discernible from their reply/written statement is that incident in question took place due to rash and negligent driving of drivers of vehicle bearing No. DL1M7272 and RJ11GA4230. The present claim petition is not maintainable as the petitioner has not arrayed drivers, owners and insurance companies of the vehicles bearing No. DL1M7272 and RJ11GA4230 as party in the present claim petition. The alleged offending vehicle has been falsely implicated in the present matter by the police in connivance with petitioner. Driver of the averred offending vehicle late Sh. Shiv Babu was holding a valid and effective driving license. Respondents have a valid permit and fitness certificate at the time of incident. Vehicle in question was duly insured with respondent no.3 at the time of incident. The respondents no.1 & 2 denied all other averments of the petition and prayed for dismissal of the same. RESPONSE OF RESPONDENT NO.03 Ajay Pal Singh vs Ram Chandra & ors. MACT No.381/2018 Page no.5 of 25 HARVINDER by HARVINDER SINGH SINGH Date: 2024.03.11 17:04:22 +0530 4.2 Succinctly, the response of respondent no.03 as discernible from its written statement/reply is that 08 vehicles were involved in the incident in question. Only driver, owner and insurer of the vehicle No. DL1LS4071 have been made party to the petition. The present petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties. It is liable to be dismissed. Vehicle bearing registration No. DL1LS4071 was duly insured with it vide policy no. 31170131160100006676 in the name of Raj Kumar Gupta, respondent no.2 for period 18.02.2017 to 17.02.2018 covering the date of incident. With these main contentions, respondent no.3 has prayed for dismissal of the petition. ISSUES 5.1 Thereafter, matter was fixed for evidence of petitioner side. PETITIONER SIDE EVIDENCE 6. The petitioner/claimant/injured examined himself as PW1 to establish his claim. He tendered his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.PW1/A reiterating and supporting the contents of his Ajay Pal Singh vs Ram Chandra & ors. He relied upon copy of his Aadhar Card Ex.PW1/1, copy of his PAN card Ex.PW1/2, copy of his driving license Ex.PW1/3, his medical bills Ex.PW1/4 and discharge summary Ex.PW1/5 in his evidence. PW1 was cross-examined at length by Ld. Counsel for the respondent No.3/Insurance Company, not cross-examined by respondent no.1 & 2 despite opportunity granted which is not reproduced herein for the sake of brevity and was discharged. RESPONDENT SIDE EVIDENCE 7. No evidence has been led by respondents in this matter. Submissions/contentions of the petitioner side are that the petitioner side has positively proved that the incident took place due to rash and negligent driving of driver of the offending vehicle. The injured was about 44 years of age at the time of accident, was working as driver and was earning Rs.16500/- per month at the time of incident. Award may be passed by this Tribunal as per entitlement/claim of applicant/injured. 8.2 Submissions/contentions of the respondent no.01 & 02 are that the petitioner side has failed to prove that incident in question took place due to rash and negligent driving of driver of alleged offending vehicle Late Sh. Shiv Babu. Incident took place due to negligence of injured himself. Petitioner side has failed to prove the job/business/work and income of the deceased. With these main submissions/contentions, the respondent no.01 & 02 has prayed for dismissal of the Ajay Pal Singh vs Ram Chandra & ors. MACT No.381/2018 Page no.7 of 25 Submissions/contentions of the respondent no.03 are that the petitioner side has failed to prove that incident in question took place due to rash and negligent driving of deceased driver. With these main submissions/contentions, the respondent no.03 has prayed for dismissal of the petition. ANALYSIS/FINDINGS

The process would involve determination/assessment of lump-sum amounts under those heads.

In case of assessment of loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, the Tribunal needs to first ascertain whether the disability noted/assessed by the medical board is temporary or permanent in nature.
If the disability is permanent in nature, then whether it is a total permanent disablement or partial permanent disablement.
If the disablement has been referred/expressed in percentage terms, in reference to any specific limb then the effect of such disablement of the limb on the function of entire body.
Once, the permanent disability is ascertained, then the Tribunal needs to determine whether such permanent disability has affected or will affect the earning capacity of the claimant.
To ascertain same, the Tribunal needs to ascertain the avocation, profession and nature of work of the claimant before the incident.
The Tribunal also needs to ascertain his age and then needs to ascertain what activities the claimant could carry on in spite of permanent disability and what he could not do as result of same.

The Tribunal then also needs to ascertain whether the claimant is totality disabled from earning any kind of livelihood or whether in spite of the permanent disability, the claimant could still effectively carry on activities Ajay Pal Singh
After ascertaining the functional disability vide above process, then Tribunal needs to workout the loss of earning capacity per month.
The Tribunal is thereafter required to workout loss of earning capacity per annum.
An appropriate multiplier needs to be ascertained as per judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in matter of "Sarla Verma Vs. DTC" 2009 ACJ 1298 SC according to age of the injured/victim.
The total loss of earning capacity then needs to be worked out multiplying appropriate multiplier ascertained with ascertained annual loss of earning capacity.
